name: Cornflower
grown_as: A hardy annual, once a cornfield weed. William's library has three: 'Blue Diadem' (large, very full blue heads), 'Double Mixed' (blue, pink, white, purple and maroon) and the wild field cornflower in the upper orchard. Drawn as the blue wild type. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A slender, upright annual 40 to 80 cm, the wiry stems branched in the upper half, the whole plant grey and cottony.

leaf.outline: Lower leaves lance-shaped, sometimes with a few narrow side lobes; upper leaves long, narrow and grass-like, 5 to 10 cm
leaf.base: Upper leaves stalkless; lower leaves narrowing into a short stalk
leaf.margin: Smooth on the upper leaves; lower leaves with a few lobes or teeth
leaf.surface: Covered in white cobwebby wool, thickest beneath and on young growth

flower.form: A head with an outer ring of large, spreading, funnel-shaped florets round a centre of smaller ones
flower.petals: Not strap-shaped rays: each outer floret is a separate little trumpet with five to seven jagged pointed teeth at its rim, roughly 6 to 12 of them spreading out round the head
flower.centre: Smaller, upright, tubular florets, darker blue-purple, with dark stamens
flower.behind: An egg- or urn-shaped cup of overlapping green bracts, each with a fringed edge of tiny dark brown and silvery teeth, like scales
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of long, wiry branched stems, upright, above the sparse leaves

fruit: The bract cup stays closed and dries brown. Seeds oblong, smooth and shiny, pale grey, 3 to 4 mm, with a short brush of stiff reddish-brown bristles at one end.
seedling: Two smooth, thickish, oval seed leaves. The first true leaves are narrow and lance-shaped, grey and woolly.
winter: Nothing, or autumn-sown seedlings sitting as small grey rosettes.

leaf: narrow lance to grass-like leaf, smooth-edged (lower leaves may have a few lobes)
bloom: outer ring of separate trumpet-shaped florets with jagged toothed rims, not flat strap petals
egg-shaped cup of scaly green bracts with dark fringed edges behind
seed: smooth, shiny, pale grey oblong seed
short brush of brown bristles at one end
young: slender upright grey-green plant with narrow leaves
flower: slender wiry branched stems each with a blue head at the tip
sparse narrow leaves below the flowers
seedhead: closed, dry, scaly brown bract cups at the stem tips

look_alikes: Perennial cornflower (Centaurea montana) has broad leaves and a few widely spaced, very spidery outer florets. Knapweeds are purple without large outer florets (except greater knapweed, which has lobed leaves). Chicory has flat strap-shaped blue rays and flowers stuck along the stem.
